title: Harness of Minervini v2 ticker.chart response

exit_codes.0: A valid domain envelope was emitted; its status may still be partial, unavailable, or needs_input.
exit_codes.2: The request or arguments were invalid; stdout contains a needs_input error envelope.
exit_codes.3: An unexpected internal contract failure occurred; stdout contains an unavailable error envelope.

as_of.description: Completed US trading session in YYYY-MM-DD form; defaults to the latest completed regular session.

format.description: Output detail only; compact preserves verdict, signals, and missing evidence while omitting verbose basis rows.

no_cache.description: Bypass both provider-cache reads and writes for this invocation.

output_dir.description: Destination directory; defaults to the ignored .artifacts/charts directory.

limitations: Charts corroborate qualitative ambiguity but never override a deterministic hard gate. A history the measuring side will not read is refused here too rather than rendered: two definitions of a usable bar let a chart succeed off bars ticker.setup rejects, and the artifact then carried a null input digest -- the one thing a setup approval has to name.

Weekly is rendered before daily; historical as-of is enforced before rendering. A weekly bar is kept for the sessions it aggregates rather than for the Friday it is labelled with, so a week read mid-way through, or one whose Friday is a holiday, keeps its bar and its anchors instead of vanishing. Such a bar aggregates only the sessions it has, which makes its volume short for a reason that is not the stock going quiet, and the manifest flags it as last_bar_partial. Artifact paths carry the bars' own digest, so two renders of different history into one directory cannot interleave into a manifest that names one digest beside a picture drawn from another -- the digest is what a setup approval cites.

The detector's turning points and its pivot are marked on the price panel, because this is where a person turns that proposal into the approval ticker.setup asks for. A segmentation the detector will not vouch for draws nothing rather than showing a structure the engine refuses to use. Each anchor is placed on the bar containing its session -- the session itself on the daily chart, the week it fell in on the weekly -- and one the chart does not reach is left off. Every manifest artifact lists the anchors its own picture contains, so what was drawn is not inferred from what was available.

The Power Play spans are drawn too, and they are the questions ticker.power-play raises from this history rather than a structure this capability picked out for itself. That capability cannot settle the volume clause alone -- the source says an explosive move commences on huge volume and names no number -- so it issues a chart question per undecided criterion per candidate top and waits, and each question carries the whole span it is about. Read here with nothing answered, because answers live in a request and this capability is not in it: the picture is what a reader is asked before they answer, and a span they have since settled is drawn again rather than dropped. The picture shows, for every open question, where that advance began, the peak it ended on, the flag low, the quiet window the volume ratio was divided by, and the heaviest session of the advance -- as far as the question named them. A history ending on the peak has no flag low and one beginning inside the advance has no baseline, and a landmark the question did not carry is not on the picture. Each artifact reports what it drew one list per landmark, so a mark that is absent because nothing named it is distinguishable from one absent because this timeframe does not reach the session. A chain read to several tops is usually one advance, so a landmark is drawn once per bar it falls on and carries the dates of every reading that landed there, only where the readings actually differ. Counted per bar rather than per date because a weekly bar holds a week of them: deduped by date, five tops drew five stars at three positions with five legend entries behind them, and the legend is the only thing binding a mark to the question key it answers. A mark that stands for more than one reading sits where that bar's readings reached -- the highest of the tops, the lowest of the flag lows -- and prints no volume multiple where they divided by different baselines. Every value comes from the question, so the two cannot describe different tops with the same digest on both -- which is what happened when this capability measured its own: it drew the highest top while the question was about a lower one, and the seam accepted the answer. The ratio is printed only on the daily panel: it divides one session's volume by a session baseline, and a weekly bar is five of them added together, so the weekly marks which week holds that session and states no multiple. Nothing is drawn when nothing is being asked, and this capability holds no opinion about whether a structure deserves the question. The overlay names its own input beside itself, in power_play.measured_bars: input_sha256 covers the five price columns, which identifies the candles but not this overlay, since a split or a payout inside a span changes which questions exist without touching a price. Two histories differing only there once produced two questions and a chart with no span at all, digests matching on both, and the answer read off that blank picture was accepted. It is null where the history never said whether a split occurred, which is where no question is issued either.
x-capability-contract.output: Chart artifact paths plus an input-hash manifest recording ticker, as-of, timeframe order, completed-bar provenance, the swing segmentation drawn on the price panel, and a power_play block holding the spans drawn from ticker.power-play's open questions with the two digests they were drawn and measured from.
side_effects: Writes deterministic PNG artifacts and a manifest to the requested directory; the default directory is git-ignored.

status_meanings.needs_input: The destination path or ticker is invalid, or that directory already holds a different render under the name this one would take -- two inputs whose truncated digests met, which a different --output-dir settles.
status_meanings.ok: Both chart artifacts and the manifest were written.
status_meanings.partial: Completed price history stops before the requested session, so no artifact is written.
status_meanings.unavailable: Completed price history is unavailable, or the history the provider returned is not renderable -- the reason names which, in the same vocabulary ticker.swings uses, because a caller told only that something failed cannot tell a data problem from a bug.

x-capability-contract.summary: Render auditable weekly-first and daily chart artifacts from the same completed bars used by deterministic analysis.
